title: Georgia Declares State Sovereignty from the Soviet Union
note: The Supreme Soviet of the Georgian SSR adopted the sovereignty resolution on 9 March 1990, condemning the 1921 Soviet annexation as illegal. Date and framing confirmed.

title: First Multi-Party Elections in Soviet Georgia
note: Elections held 28 October 1990 (second round 11 November). Round Table–Free Georgia led by Gamsakhurdia won 155 of 250 seats. All facts confirmed.

title: South Ossetia Conflict Erupts into Armed Clashes
note: Armed conflict began January 1991 after Georgia abolished South Ossetia's autonomous status in December 1990 (not 1991 as implied). The autonomous status revocation was late 1990; fighting started January 1991. Description is essentially correct.

title: Independence Referendum Approved by 99% of Voters
note: Held 31 March 1991. Official result 98.9–99.5% in favor (minor source variation), turnout 90.6%. The title says '99%' which matches rounded official figures.

title: Georgia Formally Declares Independence from the USSR
note: Act of Restoration of State Independence adopted 9 April 1991, two years after the 1989 Tbilisi massacre. Georgia was first non-Baltic Soviet republic to declare independence. All facts confirmed.

title: Zviad Gamsakhurdia Elected First President of Georgia
note: Election held 26 May 1991. Gamsakhurdia received 86–88% depending on source (event says 86%, within range). Confirmed as first direct presidential election.

title: Military Coup Overthrows President Gamsakhurdia
note: Coup ran 22 December 1991 to 6 January 1992. Kitovani and Ioseliani led the paramilitary forces. Gamsakhurdia fled 2 January 1992. Military Council took power. All facts confirmed.

title: Eduard Shevardnadze Returns to Lead Georgia
note: Shevardnadze returned March 1992 and was appointed head of the State Council. Former Soviet Foreign Minister framing confirmed.

title: War in Abkhazia Begins with Georgian Military Intervention
note: Georgian forces entered Abkhazia on 14 August 1992, ostensibly to protect rail infrastructure. 13-month conflict confirmed. All key facts match.

title: Fall of Sukhumi and Ethnic Cleansing of Georgians from Abkhazia
note: Sukhumi fell 27 September 1993. Displacement figure given as 200,000–250,000; event states 'over 200,000', consistent. All key facts confirmed.

title: Georgia Joins the Commonwealth of Independent States
note: Shevardnadze announced readiness to join CIS on 8 October 1993 under Russian pressure during Abkhazia war. The framing and date are confirmed.

title: Zviad Gamsakhurdia Dies Under Disputed Circumstances
note: Died 31 December 1993 in western Georgia. Official ruling of suicide (gunshot) remains disputed; family and investigators have questioned it. All facts confirmed.

title: Ceasefire Agreement Freezes Abkhazia Conflict
note: Moscow Agreement on Cease-fire signed 14 May 1994. CIS (Russian) peacekeeping forces deployed to Gali security zone. All facts confirmed.

title: Hyperinflation Peaks at Over 15,000%
note: Monthly inflation exceeded 60% in first three quarters of 1994; annualised this exceeds 15,000%. IMF data confirms catastrophic hyperinflation peaked in 1994. Claim is consistent.

title: New Constitution Adopted Establishing Presidential Republic
note: Constitution adopted by parliament on 24 August 1995 by 159–8 vote, entered into force 17 October 1995. All facts confirmed.

title: Georgian Lari Replaces Hyperinflated Coupon Currency
note: The lari was introduced 25 September 1995 (not October 2 as stated in the event — October 2 was the date coins entered circulation). Exchange rate 1 lari = 1,000,000 coupons confirmed. Minor date discrepancy; year is correct.

title: Shevardnadze Wins Presidential Election
note: Shevardnadze won November 1995 presidential election. ~75% vote share confirmed. International observers noted progress despite irregularities.

title: Georgia Establishes GUAM Regional Alliance
note: GUAM founded 10 October 1997 at the Council of Europe summit in Strasbourg. Georgia, Ukraine, Azerbaijan, Moldova. All facts confirmed.

title: Georgia Joins the Council of Europe
note: Georgia joined the Council of Europe on 27 April 1999 as its 41st member state. Date and framing confirmed.

title: Pankisi Gorge Crisis Escalates Tensions with Russia
note: Crisis peaked in 2001–2002. Russian cross-border airstrikes occurred in 2002, not 2001 as described. Event year 2001 is when tensions began escalating; airstrikes were 2002. Description broadly accurate but slightly compresses the timeline.

title: Rose Revolution Ousts President Shevardnadze
note: Disputed parliamentary elections 2 November 2003; Shevardnadze resigned 23 November 2003. Saakashvili led protesters into parliament on 22 November. All facts confirmed.

title: Mikheil Saakashvili Inaugurated as President
note: Inaugurated 25 January 2004, elected 4 January 2004 with 96% of vote. Event states he was 36; he was 36 at election and 37 at inauguration (born 21 December 1967). Minor age discrepancy. Described as 'youngest European head of state' — confirmed.

title: Ajara Crisis Resolved Peacefully Under Saakashvili
note: May 2004 crisis; Abashidze fled to Russia; central authority restored without bloodshed. All facts confirmed.

title: Sweeping Anti-Corruption and Police Reform Launched
note: Traffic police dissolved and rebuilt from scratch under Saakashvili's 2004 reforms. Transparency International ranking improved significantly. All facts confirmed.

title: Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan Oil Pipeline Inaugurated
note: Pipeline inaugurated at Sangachal 25 May 2005; Georgian section inaugurated 12 October 2005. First oil reached Ceyhan in June 2006. Event year 2005 reflects the inauguration, which is accurate.

title: Russia Imposes Trade Embargo and Deports Georgians
note: Wine/mineral water/agricultural bans began March–May 2006. Mass deportations followed spy row in October 2006. All facts confirmed.

title: South Ossetia Holds Unrecognized Independence Referendum
note: Referendum held 12 November 2006. ~99% voted for independence; not recognized internationally. All facts confirmed.

title: November Protests and Crackdown in Tbilisi
note: November 2007 protests in Tbilisi; tear gas and water cannons used; state of emergency declared; snap presidential election called. All facts confirmed.

title: Russia-Georgia War Over South Ossetia
note: War began 7–8 August 2008; five days of fighting; Russian forces advanced toward Tbilisi; French-brokered ceasefire. All facts confirmed.

title: Sarkozy-Brokered Six-Point Ceasefire Agreement Signed
note: Ceasefire negotiated 12 August 2008; signed/implemented by 15–16 August. Sarkozy acting for EU presidency confirmed. All facts confirmed.

title: Russia Recognizes Independence of Abkhazia and South Ossetia
note: Russia recognized both territories on 26 August 2008 and established permanent military bases. International community condemned the move. All facts confirmed.

title: NATO Bucharest Summit Promises Future Membership for Georgia
note: April 2008 Bucharest summit declared Georgia and Ukraine would eventually become NATO members but denied MAP. Considered a factor in the August war. All facts confirmed.

title: Georgia Withdraws from the Commonwealth of Independent States
note: Georgia's withdrawal from the CIS took effect 18 August 2009, one year after its post-war announcement. First country to leave the CIS confirmed.

title: Constitutional Reform Shifts to Parliamentary System
note: Constitutional amendments adopted October 2010, reduced presidential powers, strengthened PM and parliament, effective after 2013 presidential transition. All facts confirmed.

title: Georgian Dream Coalition Wins Parliamentary Elections
note: October 2012 election; Georgian Dream led by Ivanishvili defeated UNM. First peaceful electoral transfer of power in Georgia confirmed.

title: Prison Abuse Scandal Shocks Georgia
note: Videos released 18 September 2012 showing torture and sexual abuse at Gldani No. 8 Prison; broadcast on TV9. All facts confirmed.

title: Giorgi Margvelashvili Elected President
note: October 2013 presidential election; Georgian Dream candidate Margvelashvili won with over 62% of the vote. All facts confirmed.

title: EU-Georgia Association Agreement Signed
note: Signed 27 June 2014; includes DCFTA. Entered fully into force 1 July 2016. All facts confirmed.

title: Catastrophic Tbilisi Flood Kills 20 and Devastates Zoo
note: Flash flood 13–14 June 2015 along Vere River; at least 20 deaths including 3 zoo workers. Zoo lost 300+ animals. Event says '22,000 lost electricity' — not confirmed in search but rest of facts match. Core facts verified.

title: Georgian Dream Wins Supermajority in Parliament
note: Georgian Dream won 115 of 150 seats in October 2016, securing constitutional supermajority. All facts confirmed.

title: EU Grants Visa-Free Travel to Georgian Citizens
note: Visa-free travel came into force 28 March 2017. All facts confirmed.

title: Constitutional Amendments Transition to Fully Parliamentary System
note: 2017 constitutional reforms abolished direct presidential elections in favor of parliamentary appointment and moved to fully proportional system by 2024. All facts confirmed.

title: Salome Zourabichvili Elected as Last Directly Elected President
note: Won December 2018 runoff; first female president; last president elected by popular vote before shift to parliamentary appointment. All facts confirmed.

title: Gavrilov Night Protests Erupt Over Russian Lawmaker Visit
note: 20 June 2019; Russian Duma member Sergei Gavrilov sat in parliament speaker's chair. Protests dispersed with rubber bullets; 275 people injured (event says 'over 240' — slight undercount). Russia imposed flight ban. Minor number discrepancy.

title: Disputed Parliamentary Elections Trigger Opposition Boycott
note: October 2020 elections; opposition boycotted parliament; EU mediation by Charles Michel led to April 2021 compromise. All facts confirmed.

title: Georgia Applies for EU Membership
note: Application submitted 3 March 2022, days after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Ukraine and Moldova applied simultaneously. All facts confirmed.

title: Foreign Influence Law Withdrawn After Mass Protests
note: March 2023 foreign agents bill sparked mass protests; government withdrew the bill. All facts confirmed.

title: EU Grants Georgia Candidate Status with Conditions
note: European Council granted candidate status 14–15 December 2023 conditional on reforms. All facts confirmed.

title: Foreign Agents Law Enacted Despite Massive Protests
note: Parliament passed law May 2024; president vetoed; veto overridden; law entered force August 2024. Protests up to 100,000 confirmed. EU froze accession process. All facts confirmed.

title: Disputed October Parliamentary Elections Trigger Crisis
note: Elections 26 October 2024; opposition and international observers alleged fraud; massive protests followed; opposition boycotted new parliament. All facts confirmed.

title: Georgian Dream Suspends EU Accession Talks
note: PM Kobakhidze announced suspension on 28 November 2024 (event says 28 November — confirmed). Talks suspended until 2028. Triggered massive protests. All facts confirmed.

title: President Zourabichvili Refuses to Vacate Office
note: As of September 2025 Zourabichvili still refuses to stand down, declared the October 2024 elections fraudulent and continues performing presidential functions from a new Tbilisi office. All facts confirmed.

title: Expanded Foreign Agents Law Introduces Criminal Penalties
note: New Foreign Agents Registration Act came into force 1 June 2025 with criminal penalties including up to 5 years imprisonment. Broader than 2024 law. All facts confirmed.
